Pemenuhan tanggung jawab terhadap lingkungan juga diwujudkan Bank dengan mengoptimalkan operasional kantor yang ramah lingkungan dengan mengedepankan prinsip 3R (Reduce, Reuse & Recycle). Prinsip tersebut diimplementasikan dalam pengelolaan penggunaan kertas, energi listrik, bahan bakar minyak, air/air limbah maupun limbah, baik limbah yang termasuk dalam Bahan Berbahaya dan Beracun (B3) maupun non-B3B sesuai dengan regulasi yang berlaku. Jika pun dalam laporan ini terdapat kenaikan penggunaan kertas, energi, emisi dan air, hal itu dipengaruhi oleh meningkatnya operasional Bank, termasuk di antaranya penambahan karyawan.

Kinerja Aspek Sosial

Tanggung jawab pada aspek sosial dilaksanakan Bank dengan menjawab dan memenuhi berbagai keperluan dan harapan para pemangku kepentingan, baik internal maupun eksternal. Untuk karyawan, Bank dengan konsisten memperlakukan karyawan secara setara sehingga tidak terjadi insiden diskriminasi, memenuhi hak-hak normatif sesuai regulasi ketenagakerjaan, memberikan peluang yang sama untuk maju dan berkembang melalui keikutsertaan berbagai pendidikan dan pelatihan, serta mewujudkan lingkungan kerja yang sehat dan aman sesuai kaidah Kesehatan dan Keselamatan Kerja (K3).

Terkhusus untuk pengembangan kompetensi karyawan, pada tahun 2024, Bank telah menyelenggarakan pengembangan kompetensi sebanyak 179 program, yang diikuti oleh 439 pegawai atau 93% dari total pegawai dengan jumlah jam pelatihan sebanyak 1.472 jam. Adapun biaya pengembangan kompetensi tercatat sebesar Rp4,853 miliar naik dibandingkan tahun 2023, yang mencapai Rp3,886 miliar. Sementara itu, untuk kinerja K3, Bank berhasil mempertahankan pencapaian tahun sebelumnya yaitu tidak tercatat adanya kecelakaan kerja dan penyakit akibat kerja.

Adapun pemenuhan tanggung jawab kepada nasabah sebagai salah satu pemangku kepentingan eksternal utama, Bank secara berkelanjutan melakukan inovasi produk dan jasa agar sesuai dengan harapan terkini. Selain itu, Bank juga mengoptimalkan layanan agar semakin efektif dan efisien, serta memudahkan nasabah bertransaksi di manapun dan kapanpun. Lebih dari itu, sebagai bagian dari layanan terbaik serta perlindungan terhadap nasabah, Bank juga berkomitmen untuk menyelesaikan semua pengaduan nasabah sesuai dengan Service Level Agreement (SLA) yang berlaku. Berdasarkan survei internal yang diadakan Bank kepada nasabah, sebanyak 78,56% nasabah menyatakan puas dengan produk dan layanan Bank.

Komitmen lain yang senantiasa dipegang Bank adalah menjaga dan melindungi kerahasiaan data nasabah agar tidak ada yang bocor, apalagi hilang. Upaya tersebut berhasil dipertahankan sebagaimana tahun sebelumnya, yang ditandai dengan tidak adanya pengaduan berkaitan dengan kebocoran data atau hilangnya data nasabah.

The Bank also realized its environmental responsibility by optimizing environmentally friendly office operations. It did this by prioritizing the “3R” principle (Reduce, Reuse & Recycle). This principle was implemented in the Bank through its management of paper use, electrical energy, fuel oil, waste water and waste, whether it was waste categorized as “Hazardous and Toxic Materials” or non-Hazardous and Toxic Materials. It carried out all of this in accordance with applicable regulations. Any increase mentioned in this report in the Bank's use of paper, energy, emissions and water was influenced by an increase in the Bank's operations, including its addition of employees.

Social Aspect Performance

The Bank carried out its social responsibility by responding to (and fulfilling the various needs and expectations of) both internal and external stakeholders. For employees, the Bank consistently treated its employees equally so that there were no incidents of discrimination. It also fulfilled all normative rights in accordance with employment regulations, provided equal opportunities for employees to advance and develop through participation in various education sessions and training activities, and created a healthy and safe work environment that operated in accordance with Occupational Health and Safety principles.

Specifically, in terms of employee competency development, the Bank organized 179 competency development programs in 2024 that were attended by 439 employees (or 93% of the Bank's total employees) with a total of 1,472 training hours. The Bank's competency development cost was recorded at IDR4.853 billion, an increase compared to IDR3.886 billion in 2023. Meanwhile, in terms of Occupational Health and Safety performance, the Bank managed to maintain its previous year's achievement of having no work accidents or work-related diseases being recorded.

In terms of fulfilling its responsibilities to customers as one of its primary external stakeholders, the Bank worked to continuously innovate its products and services to meet current expectations. In addition, the Bank also optimized services to be more effective and efficient, and made it easier for customers to transact anywhere and anytime. Moreover, as part of its best service and protection for customers, the Bank also committed itself to resolving all customer complaints in accordance with applicable Service Level Agreements (SLA). Based on Bank's own internal survey to customers, some 78.56% of customers expressed satisfaction with the Bank's products and services.

Another commitment that the Bank always upheld was its effort to maintain and protect the confidentiality of customer data so that nothing is ever leaked, let alone lost. The Bank was able to successfully maintain this level of data security as it had in the previous year, which was a year marked by the absence of complaints related to data leaks or any losses of customer data.

# Prospek dan Peluang

Pada tahun 2025, perekonomian Indonesia diproyeksikan tumbuh stabil di kisaran 5%. Bank Dunia dalam laporannya pada Oktober 2024 memperkirakan pertumbuhan sebesar 5,1% untuk tahun 2025. Sementara itu, Pemerintah Indonesia sebagaimana disampaikan dalam Anggaran Pendapatan dan Belanja Negara Tahun 2025 menargetkan pertumbuhan ekonomi sebesar 5,2%. Di sisi lain, pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia tahun 2025 akan menghadapi berbagai kendala dan tantangan di antaranya defisit transaksi berjalan yang diperkirakan melebar antara 0,5% hingga 1,3% dari PDB, serta terjadinya penyusutan kelas menengah yang dapat mempengaruhi konsumsi domestik.

Di tengah proyeksi optimistis, sekaligus tantangan yang patut diwaspadai, industri perbankan Indonesia diharapkan tetap solid dan berperan aktif dalam mendukung pertumbuhan ekonomi tahun 2025. Dalam hal ini, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) optimistis terhadap kinerja positif sektor jasa keuangan, meskipun menghadapi tantangan likuiditas yang dapat mempengaruhi penyaluran kredit. Bank Indonesia memproyeksikan pertumbuhan kredit perbankan akan meningkat menjadi 11-13% pada tahun 2025, lebih tinggi dibandingkan proyeksi tahun sebelumnya.

Berdasarkan latar belakang dan proyeksi tersebut, Allo Bank telah menetapkan berbagai target dalam RBB Tahun 2025, terkhusus pada aspek ekonomi, serta rencana strategis untuk mencapainya. Target tersebut di antaranya Laba Bersih sebesar Rp466 miliar; Kredit yang Diberikan sebesar Rp9,7 triliun atau 130% dibandingkan realisasi tahun 2024, dan Dana Pihak Ketiga sebesar Rp8,4 triliun atau 138% dibandingkan realisasi tahun 2024.

Selaras dengan penetapan tersebut, Allo Bank telah menetapkan berbagai inisiatif strategis dan berkomitmen untuk melaksanakannya secara konsisten dengan menguatkan sinergi antara manajemen dan karyawan. Berbekal spirit untuk memberikan kontribusi terbaik, Allo Bank optimistis dapat mencapai target-target tersebut demi mewujudkan bisnis yang berkelanjutan.

# Prospects and Opportunities

In 2025, the Indonesian economy is projected to grow steadily in the range of 5%. In its October 2024 report, the World Bank specifically estimated a total growth of 5.1% for 2025. Meanwhile, the Government of Indonesia has stated in its 2025 State Budget that it is targeting an economic growth of 5.2%. At the same time, Indonesia's economic growth in 2025 is set to face various obstacles and challenges, including its current account deficit, which is estimated to widen between 0.5% and 1.3% of GDP, as well as a shrinking middle class that could affect domestic consumption.

In the midst of these optimistic projections, as well as in the midst of challenges that should continue to be monitored, the Indonesian banking industry is expected to remain in solid condition and continue to play an active role in supporting economic growth in 2025. In this regard, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) is optimistic about the positive performance of the financial services sector in the face of liquidity challenges that could affect credit distribution. Bank Indonesia projects that banking credit growth will increase to 11-13% in 2025, higher than the previous year's projections.

With all of these projections in mind, Allo Bank has set various targets in its 2025 RBB, specifically when it comes to the economic aspects. It has also established strategic plans for how to achieve these targets. The targets include Net Profit of IDR466 billion; Lending of IDR9.7 trillion or 130% compared to the realization in 2024, and Third Party Funds of IDR8.4 trillion or 138% compared to the realization in 2024.

In line with these goals, Allo Bank has established various strategic initiatives and is committed to implementing them consistently. It aims to do so by strengthening its synergy between management and employees. Armed with its desire to provide the best in contributions, Allo Bank is optimistic that it can achieve its targets in order to realize its goal of sustainable business operations.

Selain menerjemahkan spirit undang-undang lingkungan, penerbitan POJK Keuangan Berkelanjutan tak lepas dari Roadmap Keuangan Berkelanjutan di Indonesia 2015-2019 yang dikeluarkan oleh Otoritas Jasa Keuangan. Selepas itu, disusul dengan terbitnya Roadmap Keuangan Berkelanjutan Tahap II (2021-2025). Fokus Roadmap Tahap II adalah mendorong terciptanya ekosistem keuangan berkelanjutan secara komprehensif dengan melibatkan seluruh pihak terkait dan mendorong pengembangan kerja sama dengan pihak lain. OJK berharap roadmap terbaru tersebut dapat menjadi landasan bagi pelaku sektor jasa keuangan, sekaligus menjadi rujukan bagi kementerian/lembaga terkait dalam mengembangkan inisiatif-inisiatif pembiayaan inovatif yang selaras dengan prinsip keuangan berkelanjutan.

Sesuai dengan Roadmap Keuangan Berkelanjutan Tahap II (2021 - 2025) yang dirilis OJK, Allo Bank sebagai salah satu perusahaan yang bergerak di industri perbankan mendukung penuh penerapan Keuangan Berkelanjutan di Indonesia. Hal ini diharapkan dapat meningkatkan daya tahan dan daya saing Bank sehingga mampu tumbuh dan berkembang secara berkesinambungan, serta berkontribusi atas permasalahan isu serta mitigasi risiko dalam hal permasalahan lingkungan hidup dan dapat terus berkontribusi secara positif pada stabilitas sistem keuangan.

Dukungan dan komitmen Bank untuk menerapkan keuangan berkelanjutan, sekaligus mendukung pembangunan berkelanjutan di Indonesia, diwujudkan dengan menyusun Rencana Aksi Keuangan Berkelanjutan (RAKB), seperti diatur dalam pasal 4 ayat (1) POJK Keuangan Berkelanjutan. According to this regulation, sustainable finance is defined as comprehensive support from the financial services sector to foster sustainable economic growth by integrating economic, social, and environmental interests.

The issuance of the POJK on Sustainable Finance has positioned financial services institutions within an environmentally friendly financial system, as mandated by Law No. 32 of 2009 on Environmental Protection and Management. Article 43, paragraph 3, letter c of the law highlights the development of an environmentally friendly financial institution and capital market system.

Beyond reflecting the spirit of environmental law, the issuance of the POJK on Sustainable Finance is also closely tied to the 2015-2019 Sustainable Finance Roadmap in Indonesia, issued by the Financial Services Authority. This was followed by the Sustainable Finance Roadmap Phase II (2021-2025), which focuses on creating a comprehensive sustainable finance ecosystem by involving all relevant parties and fostering cooperation with other parties. The OJK expects this latest roadmap to serve as a foundation for financial services sector players and as a reference for ministries and related institutions in developing innovative financing initiatives aligned with sustainable finance principles.

In accordance with the Sustainable Finance Roadmap Phase II (2021-2025) released by OJK, Allo Bank, as a banking industry player, fully supports the implementation of Sustainable Finance in Indonesia. This commitment is expected to enhance the Bank's resilience and competitiveness, enabling sustainable growth while addressing key environmental issues and mitigating related risks. Furthermore, Allo Bank aims to contribute positively to the stability of the financial system.

The Bank's commitment to sustainable finance and its support for sustainable development in Indonesia is demonstrated through the preparation of a Sustainable Finance Action Plan (RAKB), as mandated by Article 4, paragraph (1) of the POJK on Sustainable Finance. The RAKB, which is an integral part of the Bank's Business Plan (RBB), outlines strategic plans, programs, and policies as an implementation of Sustainable Finance principles.

# Tata Kelola Berkelanjutan Sustainable Governance

Tata Kelola Perusahaan yang Baik (Good Corporate Governance) memiliki peran krusial dalam industri perbankan Indonesia, terutama bagi bank umum berbasis layanan digital seperti Allo Bank. Penerapan tata kelola secara paripurna tidak hanya memperkuat posisi Bank dalam menghadapi persaingan, tetapi juga mendukung perkembangan jangka panjang dan meningkatkan kepercayaan para pemangku kepentingan. Lebih lanjut, bagi Allo Bank yang beroperasi dalam lingkungan teknologi digital yang cepat berubah, tata kelola yang baik menjadi semakin penting untuk memastikan penggunaan teknologi yang inovatif dan aman, manajemen risiko yang memadai, serta perlindungan data nasabah yang maksimal.

Allo Bank sebagai bagian dari pelaku industri perbankan berkomitmen untuk mendukung sepenuhnya penerapan tata kelola yang baik bagi bank sebagaimana disampaikan dalam POJK Tata Kelola. Dukungan direalisasikan Bank dengan menerapkan prinsip-prinsip tata kelola yaitu keterbukaan (transparency), akuntabilitas (accountability), tanggung jawab (responsibilities), independensi (independency), serta kewajaran, dan kesetaraan (fairness & equity). Untuk mendapatkan hasil terbaik, prinsip-prinsip tersebut diterapkan Bank di seluruh tingkatan atau jenjang organisasi.

Untuk mengukuhkan penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan, Bank melakukan sejumlah penyesuaian tata kelola perusahaan yang baik, yaitu tata kelola yang mengutamakan aspek Lingkungan (Environmental), Sosial (Social) dan Tata Kelola (Governance) atau ESG. ## Responsible Party in Implementing Sustainable Finance at Allo Bank

As a financial services institution and a public company, Allo Bank is obliged to comply with Financial Services Authority Regulation No. 51/POJK.03/2017 concerning the Implementation of Sustainable Finance for Financial Services Institutions, Issuers, and Public Companies (POJK Sustainable Finance). To strengthen its commitment to sustainable finance, the Bank has made a number of adjustments to its corporate governance framework by prioritizing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) aspects. These adjustments include assigning responsibility for implementing sustainable finance in accordance with Appendix II of POJK Sustainable Finance. The appendix outlines

Dalam lampiran tersebut antara lain mengatur tentang tugas anggota Direksi dan anggota Dewan Komisaris, pegawai, pejabat dan/atau unit kerja yang menjadi penanggung jawab penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan.

Di Allo Bank, penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan secara umum menjadi tanggung jawab Direktur Utama sebagai pemimpin tertinggi. Namun demikian, dalam pelaksanaan penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan, hampir seluruh pemimpin divisi yang ada di Bank turut terlibat antara lain Sekretaris Perusahaan & PMO, Funding, Kredit, HRD, Finance, Procurement & Business Planning, serta Manajemen Risiko dan Kepatuhan. [OJK E.1]

Pada tahun 2024, Bank memperoleh sertifikasi COBIT 2019 dengan Tingkat Maturitas TI di level 4,21. Keberhasilan tersebut menjadi pemenuhan salah satu komitmen dan dedikasi Bank dalam menerapkan standar terbaik dalam tata kelola teknologi informasi. Pencapaian ini merupakan bentuk keseriusan Bank dalam berinovasi secara terus menerus dan memastikan bahwa setiap proses bisnis yang menggunakan teknologi informasi berjalan dengan baik, terkontrol, dan berkelanjutan.

Secara internal Bank telah melakukan beberapa inisiatif untuk implementasi dokumentasi secara paperless telah satunya dengan penggunaan tanda tangan digital. Sehingga memungkinkan manajemen untuk menandatangani dokumen secara hemat waktu, menghemat biaya percetakan, pengiriman dan penyimpanan juga mengurangi kesalahan yang terkait dengan tanda tangan manual.

Dalam rangka peningkatan kompetensi karyawan, berbagai program training internal telah dilakukan secara daring dan sertifikat yang diberikan kepada karyawan berbentuk sertifikat secara online. Bank menggunakan KnowBe4 sebagai platform untuk melakukan training secara berkala kepada karyawan dimana karyawan bisa mendapatkan sertifikat secara online.

Memenuhi prinsip tata kelola, Bank telah melakukan pengkinian pada kebijakan penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan, dan kebijakan lain yang relevan dengan prinsip keuangan berkelanjutan. Selanjutnya Bank dalam menjalankan hubungan bisnis Bank dengan Nasabah dan pihak eksternal secara Bank wide, Bank mengedepankan prinsip kehati-hatian (Prudential Banking), beretika, juga nilai-nilai sosial yang berlaku umum.

Untuk meningkatkan awareness karyawan terhadap kebersihan di lingkungan tempat bekerja, Bank telah menetapkan kebijakan terkait tempat kerja bersih dan lingkungan kantor bersih.

Dalam hal melakukan edukasi literasi inklusi keuangan atas produk perbankan digital untuk mendukung cashless society, Bank menjadi fasilitator dan juga bekerjasama dengan berbagai institusi termasuk lembaga pendidikan.

the duties of the Board of Directors, Board of Commissioners, employees, officials, and relevant work units in implementing sustainable finance.

At Allo Bank, the overall responsibility for sustainable finance rests with the President Director as the highest-ranking leader. However, its implementation involves nearly all division leaders, including Corporate Secretary & PMO, Funding, Credit, HRD, Finance, Procurement & Business Planning, and Risk Management & Compliance. [OJK E.1]

In 2024, the Bank obtained COBIT 2019 certification with an IT Maturity Level of 4.21. This achievement reflects the Bank's commitment and dedication to implementing the highest standards in information technology governance. It also demonstrates the Bank's continuous efforts to innovate and ensure that all business processes involving information technology are well-managed, controlled, and sustainable.

Internally, the Bank has launched several initiatives to adopt paperless documentation, including the use of digital signatures. This initiative enables management to sign documents efficiently, reducing printing, shipping, and storage costs while minimizing errors associated with manual signatures.

To enhance employee competency, the Bank has conducted various internal training programs online, with certificates issued digitally. Additionally, Allo Bank utilizes the KnowBe4 platform to provide regular training sessions, allowing employees to obtain certifications online.

In alignment with governance principles, the Bank has updated its policies on sustainable finance implementation and other policies relevant to sustainable finance principles. Furthermore, in conducting business relations with customers and external parties across the Bank, it prioritizes the principle of prudence (Prudential Banking), ethics, and generally accepted social values.

To raise employee awareness about workplace cleanliness, the Bank has introduced policies promoting a clean work environment.

In terms of promoting financial inclusion and literacy education on digital banking products to support a cashless society, the Bank acts as a facilitator and collaborates with various institutions, including educational institutions.

Komitmen dan Kebijakan Tanggung Jawab Sosial Perusahaan (Corporate Social Responsibility atau "CSR") Allo Bank dalam menerapkan kegiatan tanggung jawab sosialnya mengacu pada prinsip keberlanjutan (sustainability) sebagai bentuk komitmen Bank untuk mendukung misi Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) dan membangun hubungan harmonis dengan masyarakat, lingkungan, komunitas dan seluruh pemangku kepentingan lainnya melalui perilaku yang transparan dan beretika.

CSR juga merupakan bentuk komitmen Allo Bank kepada lingkungan dengan tujuan untuk berperan serta dalam pembangunan berkelanjutan selaras dengan prinsip Triple Bottom Line yaitu People, Planet, Profit (3P) serta memberikan nilai tambah kepada semua pemangku kepentingan termasuk internal perusahaan guna mendukung pertumbuhan Bank. Allo bank mendefinisikan CSR sebagai tanggung jawab atas dampak dari keputusan dan aktivitasnya pada masyarakat dan lingkungan, melalui perilaku yang transparan dan beretika yang bertujuan untuk:

1. Membangun citra dan reputasi Bank yang dapat meningkatkan kepercayaan kepada Allo Bank
2. Membangun hubungan yang harmonis dengan segenap pemangku kepentingan.
3. Menumbuhkan positive value karyawan terhadap Allo Bank.
4. Konsisten dengan pembangunan berkelanjutan (sustainable development) dan kesejahteraan masyarakat.
5. Mematuhi peraturan dan ketentuan yang berlaku.

Allo Bank terus berupaya memaksimalkan manfaat atas keberadaan Bank di tengah masyarakat melalui berbagai program CSR di bawah branding "Allo Bank Pelita", termasuk program kerja sama dengan CT Arsa Foundation untuk semakin memperkuat dampak sosial kepada semua stakeholders.

Untuk memperkuat tata kelola yang mengutamakan ESG, sekaligus menyelaraskan dengan Rencana Aksi Keuangan Berkelanjutan (RAKB), Allo Bank melakukan tiga penyesuaian kebijakan manajemen risiko dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik sebagai berikut:

1. Melakukan pembaruan kebijakan perkreditan Bank terkait pengaturan pemberian kredit yang perlu dihindari dengan mempertimbangkan dampak aktivitas usaha yang dihasilkan dari calon debitur terhadap keberlangsungan lingkungan hidup dan dampak negatif terhadap sosial.
2. Melakukan pembaruan terhadap Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) kredit terkait penerapan Keuangan Berkelanjutan.

Regarding internal environmental responsibility, the Bank implements initiatives such as minimizing paper usage, reducing disposable food and drink containers, conserving water and electricity, and providing designated disposal areas for unused paper near printers.

Employee engagement in these initiatives is encouraged through the Culture Awareness Program, which includes email blasts to all employees, as well as Clean Desk Awareness campaigns in the form of policies and quizzes directed at all staff.

Allo Bank's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) commitment and policy in implementing its social responsibility initiatives are based on the principle of sustainability, reflecting the Bank's dedication to supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) mission. Through transparent and ethical behavior, the Bank aims to build harmonious relationships with society, the environment, communities, and all other stakeholders.

CSR is also a manifestation of Allo Bank's commitment to environmental sustainability, aligning with the Triple Bottom Line principle—People, Planet, and Profit (3P)—while delivering added value to all stakeholders, including internal entities, to support the Bank's growth. Allo Bank defines CSR as the responsibility for the impact of its decisions and activities on society and the environment, carried out through transparent and ethical practices with the following objectives:

1. Enhancing the Bank's image and reputation to strengthen public trust.
2. Building and maintaining harmonious relationships with all stakeholders.
3. Fostering positive employee value towards Allo Bank.
4. Ensuring alignment with sustainable development and community welfare.
5. Complying with applicable rules and regulations.

Allo Bank continuously strives to maximize its positive impact on society through various CSR programs under the "Allo Bank Pelita" branding, including a collaboration program with the CT Arsa Foundation, further reinforcing the Bank's social impact on all stakeholders.

To enhance governance that prioritizes ESG aspects while aligning with the Sustainable Finance Action Plan (RAKB), Allo Bank has made three adjustments to its risk management policies and corporate governance framework:

1. Updating the Bank's credit policy to include regulations on credit provisions that should be avoided, particularly those involving business activities generated by prospective debtors with negative environmental and social impacts.
2. Revising the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) pertaining to the implementation of Sustainable Finance Principles.

Penilaian Risiko Atas Penerapan Keuangan Berkelanjutan [OJK E.3]

Penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan membawa sejumlah risiko bagi perbankan yang perlu dikelola dengan cermat, termasuk tantangan dalam mengintegrasikan aspek Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG) ke dalam proses manajemen risiko. Risiko-risiko ini mencakup risiko kredit, risiko pasar, risiko likuiditas, dan risiko operasional, Selain itu, bank juga menghadapi risiko terkait perubahan iklim, yang dapat mempengaruhi kemampuan debitur untuk mengembalikan pinjaman. Untuk meminimalkan dampak atas risiko yang muncul, maka implementasi manajemen risiko menjadi sangat penting, baik yang terkait dengan fungsi identifikasi, pengukuran, pemantauan, dan pengendalian risiko yang dihadapi bank, termasuk dalam menerapkan berbagai program keuangan berkelanjutan.

Untuk meraih hasil terbaik, Allo Bank menerapkan manajemen risiko dengan mengacu pada Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan No. 18/POJK.03/2016 dan Surat Edaran Otoritas Jasa Keuangan No. 34/SEOJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum. Kerangka kerja manajemen risiko Bank menetapkan pendekatan pengelolaan risiko dan kerangka pengendalian di mana risiko dikelola untuk mendapatkan keseimbangan antara risiko (risk) dan pendapatan (return).

Allo Bank menerapkan kerangka kerja manajemen risiko melalui perumusan tingkat risiko yang akan diambil (risk appetite) dan toleransi risiko (risk tolerance) bagi setiap jenis risiko. Selain itu, Bank juga mengembangkan kebijakan dan prosedur manajemen risiko yang berkesesuaian serta pengembangan struktur pengendalian internal secara terpadu. Lebih dari itu, Bank juga membangun budaya risiko yang menitikberatkan kesadaran seluruh pegawai akan risiko dan efektivitas proses manajemen risiko.

Adapun penerapan manajemen risiko di Allo Bank mengacu pada empat pilar manajemen risiko sebagai berikut:

1. Pengawasan aktif Dewan Komisaris dan Direksi.
2. Kecukupan kebijakan, prosedur, dan penetapan limit manajemen risiko.
3. Kecukupan proses identifikasi, pengukuran, pemantauan, dan pengendalian risiko serta sistem informasi manajemen risiko.
4. Sistem pengendalian internal yang menyeluruh.

Selain mengacu keempat pilar di atas, manajemen risiko Allo Bank juga merujuk pada best practices yang dikeluarkan oleh Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.

Di sepanjang tahun 2024, segenap manajemen dengan dukungan karyawan Allo Bank secara konsisten menerapkan manajemen risiko terpadu dan komprehensif sehingga mampu mendukung pencapaian target kinerja dan menjaga kelangsungan usaha. Bank optimis penerapan strategi manajemen risiko yang proaktif akan meningkatkan efektivitas penggunaan modal dan tingkat pengembangan modal (Return on Equity) sehingga dapat memberikan nilai tambah bagi pemegang saham.

Risk Assessment on Sustainable Finance Implementation [OJK E.3]

The implementation of sustainable finance introduces various risks that banks must manage carefully, including the challenge of integrating Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) aspects into the risk management process. These risks include credit risk, market risk, liquidity risk, and operational risk. Additionally, banks face climate change-related risks that may impact borrowers' ability to repay loans. To mitigate the impact of these emerging risks, a strong risk management framework is essential, encompassing the identification, measurement, monitoring, and control of risks, including those associated with various sustainable finance programs.

To ensure effective risk management, Allo Bank adheres to Financial Services Authority Regulation No. 18/POJK.03/2016 and Financial Services Authority Circular Letter No. 34/SEOJK.03/2016 concerning the Implementation of Risk Management for Conventional Bank. The Bank's risk management framework is designed to establish a structured approach to risk control, balancing risk and return to optimize decision-making.

Allo Bank implements a risk management framework by defining the level of risk it is willing to take (risk appetite) and establishing risk tolerance for each type of risk. In addition, the Bank develops appropriate risk management policies and procedures while strengthening its integrated internal control structure. Moreover, the Bank fosters a risk-aware culture, emphasizing the importance of risk awareness among all employees and the effectiveness of the risk management process.

The Bank's risk management is structured around four key pillars:

1. Active supervision by the Board of Commissioners and Board of Directors.
2. Adequate risk management policies, procedures, and limits for risk control.
3. Effective risk identification, measurement, monitoring, and control processes, supported by an advanced risk management information system.
4. A comprehensive internal control system.

In addition to these pillars, Allo Bank aligns its risk management practices with international best practices issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.

Throughout 2024, with the support of its employees, Allo Bank consistently implemented an integrated and comprehensive risk management framework to ensure the achievement of performance targets and business continuity. The Bank remains optimistic that a proactive risk management strategy will enhance capital efficiency and optimize Return on Equity (ROE), ultimately creating added value for shareholders.

# Hubungan dengan Pemangku Kepentingan [OJK E.4]

Komunikasi dan hubungan yang harmonis antara Allo Bank dengan segenap pemangku kepentingan, baik pemangku internal maupun eksternal, merupakan pondasi yang kokoh untuk mewujudkan kinerja terbaik. Merujuk pada Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (POJK) No. 17 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Tata Kelola Bagi Bank Umum (POJK Tata Kelola), pemangku kepentingan adalah seluruh pihak yang memiliki kepentingan secara langsung atau tidak langsung terhadap kegiatan usaha Bank. Berdasarkan pengertian tersebut, Allo Bank merumuskan pemangku kepentingan sebagai kelompok atau individu yang terpengaruh oleh kegiatan, produk dan jasa yang ditawarkan Bank. Allo Bank secara berkesinambungan melibatkan para pemangku kepentingan sejalan dengan komitmen untuk meningkatkan transparansi, akuntabilitas, serta mendapatkan masukan berharga untuk perbaikan kinerja dan pengembangan produk/layanan yang sesuai kebutuhan nasabah. Lebih dari itu, pelibatan pemangku kepentingan juga penting dalam mendukung implementasi keuangan berkelanjutan dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik di Bank.

In executing its risk management strategy, the Bank conducts risk profile assessments, covering both inherent risk evaluations and risk management quality assessments. To further strengthen risk management, Allo Bank is committed to improving composite rating assessments through continuous evaluation and refinement of the four primary risks it faces: credit risk, market risk, liquidity risk, operational risk. # SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE

## Overview of Global and National Economy

Global economic growth in 2024 is expected to slow compared to 2023. According to the World Economic Outlook Update released by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in April 2024, global economic growth is projected at 3.2% for 2024, down from 3.3% in 2023. This slowdown is attributed to several factors, including tighter monetary policies in developed countries and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties.

Despite the challenging global economic conditions, the economies of several of Indonesia's key trading partners continued to grow. Singapore recorded a 4.0% growth rate, a significant increase from 1.1% in 2023. Malaysia expanded by 5.1% (2023: 3.6%), while South Korea's economy grew by 2.0% (2023: 1.4%). Meanwhile, China's economy grew by 5.0%, slowing from 5.4% in 2023. A similar trend was observed in the United States, where economic growth stood at 2.8% in 2024, slowing down compared to 2.9% in the previous year.

According to data from the Central Statistics Agency (BPS), Indonesia's economy in 2024 grew by 5.03%, slightly lower than the 5.05% recorded in 2023. From a production perspective, the main contributors to economic growth in 2024 were the Manufacturing, Construction, and Trade sectors, supported by increased production activities and rising foreign demand. The business sectors with the highest growth included Other Services, Transportation & Warehousing, and Accommodation & Food & Beverage.

Selain itu, kebijakan moneter yang lebih ketat dan pengetatan regulasi di sektor keuangan membuat lembaga keuangan harus lebih berhati-hati dalam mengelola risiko dan pinjaman sehingga mempengaruhi laju ekspansi produk dan layanan keuangan. Di sisi lain, pergeseran perilaku konsumen yang menjadi lebih selektif dan konservatif dalam mengambil keputusan finansial juga menambah beban industri jasa keuangan dalam mempertahankan pertumbuhan yang sebelumnya lebih dinamis.

Berkaitan dengan kinerja sektor jasa keuangan, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) menilai stabilitas sektor ini terjaga stabil di tengah dinamika perekonomian global dan domestik. Di sisi lain, Dana Pihak Ketiga (DPK) perbankan tercatat tumbuh sebesar 7,54% yoy (Oktober 2024: 6,74 persen yoy) menjadi Rp8.835,9 triliun, dengan giro, tabungan, dan deposito masing-masing tumbuh sebesar 10,97%, 6,55%, dan 5,57% yoy. Sementar itu, likuiditas industri perbankan pada November 2024 tetap memadai dengan rasio Alat Likuid/Non-Core Deposit (AL/NCD) dan Alat Likuid/Dana Pihak Ketiga (AL/DPK) masing-masing sebesar 112,94% (Oktober 2024: 113,64%) dan 25,57% (Oktober 2024: 25,58%) dan masih di atas threshold masing-masing sebesar 50% dan 10%. Despite the slight deceleration, Indonesia's economic growth in 2024 remains within the range projected by various global economic institutions. Banking Industry Performance in 2024

According to the BPS, Indonesia's economic growth in 2024 was supported by the expansion of all business sectors, including financial services, which grew by 4.74%, slightly slower than the 4.77% growth recorded in 2023. The slowdown was influenced by various factors, including global economic uncertainty and external pressures such as exchange rate fluctuations and a decline in foreign investment, which also impacted liquidity and investment interest within the country. Additionally, tighter monetary policies and stricter financial regulations compelled financial institutions to adopt a more cautious approach in risk and loan management, thereby affecting the pace of expansion in financial products and services. Moreover, shifting consumer behavior, with a more selective and conservative approach to financial decisions, further contributed to the challenges faced by the financial services industry in maintaining its previous growth momentum.

Despite these challenges, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) assessed that the stability of the financial services sector remained intact amid the dynamics of both the global and domestic economy. Several banking sector indicators reinforced this positive outlook. Banking intermediation performance showed continued growth, supported by a stable risk profile. As of November 2024, credit growth remained in double digits at 10.79% year-on-year (yoy), compared to 10.92% in October 2024, bringing total credit disbursement to IDR7,717 trillion.

By type of credit usage, Investment Loan recorded the highest growth at 13.77%, followed by Consumer Loan at 10.94%, while Working Capital Loan grew by 8.92%. Based on the debtor category, corporate loan expanded by 16.19%, while MSME credit also continued to grow, increasing by 4.02%.

Meanwhile, Third-Party Funds (TPF) in the banking sector grew by 7.54% yoy (October 2024: 6.74% yoy) to IDR8,835.9 trillion, with current, savings, and time deposits growing by 10.97%, 6.55%, and 5.57% yoy, respectively. The banking sector's liquidity remained adequate in November 2024, with the ratio of Liquid Assets to Non-Core Deposits (AL/NCD) and Liquid Assets to Third-Party Funds (AL/TPF) standing at 112.94% (October 2024: 113.64%) and 25.57% (October 2024: 25.58%), respectively—well above the minimum thresholds of 50% and 10%. The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) was reported at 213.07%.

OJK juga mencatat kualitas kredit tetap terjaga dengan rasio NPL gross sebesar 2,19% (Oktober 2024: 2,20%) dan NPL net sebesar 0,75% (Oktober 2024: 0,77%). Loan at Risk (LaR) juga menunjukkan tren penurunan menjadi sebesar 9,82% (Oktober 2024: 9,94%). Rasio LaR tersebut sudah lebih rendah dibandingkan sebelum pandemi yaitu sebesar 9,93% pada Desember 2019. Secara umum, tingkat profitabilitas bank (ROA) sebesar 2,69% (Oktober 2024: 2,73%), yang menunjukkan kinerja industri perbankan tetap resilien dan stabil.

Lebih lanjut, ketahanan perbankan juga tetap kuat tecermin dari permodalan (CAR) yang berada di level tinggi yaitu sebesar 26,92% (Oktober 2024: 27,02%), meskipun sedikit menurun didorong oleh pertumbuhan ATMR yang sejalan dengan pertumbuhan kredit. Permodalan perbankan yang solid menjadi bantalan mitigasi risiko yang kuat di tengah kondisi ketidakpastian global.

Rencana dan Kebijakan Strategis Bank Tahun 2024

Industri perbankan nasional menghadapi berbagai tantangan di sepanjang tahun 2024. Selain ketepatan dalam memanfaatkan kebijakan pemerintah untuk pemulihan ekonomi pasca pandemi atau post pandemic policy responses, perbankan juga menghadapi tantangan berupa spillover effect tensi geopolitik yang masih tinggi. Sumber resmi Otoritas Jasa Keuangan menyatakan kondisi tersebut mendorong volatilitas harga komoditas dan energi, lonjakan inflasi dan kenaikan suku bunga era higher for longer, serta adanya potensi perlambatan ekonomi.

Tantangan berikutnya adalah perkembangan yang sangat luar biasa dalam konteks digitalization berupa percepatan digitalisasi dan emerging technology serta aspek kesiapan industri baik dari sisi people, dari proses, maupun teknologi. Tantangan yang tak kalah penting adalah risiko keuangan terkait dengan iklim (climate related risks) serta upaya untuk mencapai target net zero emission.

Menghadapi berbagai tantangan tersebut, Allo Bank mengimplementasikan sejumlah strategi inovatif untuk memastikan pertumbuhan yang berkelanjutan. Salah satu langkah kunci adalah memperkuat kolaborasi dengan berbagai mitra strategis di dalam maupun di luar ekosistem CT Corpora, yang memungkinkan Bank untuk memanfaatkan basis pelanggan yang luas. Melalui penerapan model open banking, Allo Bank berupaya untuk meningkatkan layanan finansialnya sehingga memberikan kemudahan bagi nasabah dalam bertransaksi di era digital.

Selaras dengan itu, Bank secara konsisten mendayagunakan infrastruktur phygital (physical and digital) yang memberikan berbagai macam keuntungan bagi nasabah. Dalam hal ini, infrastruktur phygital Allo Bank menggabungkan aplikasi Mobile Banking Allo Bank dengan jaringan kanal fisik antara lain TransMart, Metro, Mitra Bukalapak, dan Indomaret.

Sesuai dengan Rencana Bisnis Bank, selama tahun 2024, Allo Bank fokus pada pengembangan beberapa ekosistem utama melalui akselerasi adopsi teknologi & transformasi digital. Melalui OJK also reported that credit quality remained well-managed, with a gross Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio of 2.19% (October 2024: 2.20%) and a net NPL of 0.75% (October 2024: 0.77%). The Loan at Risk (LaR) ratio showed a downward trend, decreasing to 9.82% in November 2024 (October 2024: 9.94%). Notably, this ratio was lower than the pre-pandemic level of 9.93% recorded in December 2019. Overall, banking profitability, as measured by Return on Assets (ROA), stood at 2.69% (October 2024: 2.73%), indicating that the banking industry remains resilient and stable.

Furthermore, the banking sector's capital resilience remained strong, as reflected in the high Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of 26.92% (October 2024: 27.02%). Although slightly lower due to an increase in ATMR driven by credit growth, the sector's solid capital base continues to serve as a robust risk mitigation buffer amid ongoing global uncertainties.

Equally important were climate-related financial risks and efforts to achieve the net-zero emissions target.

Through the implementation of the open banking model, Allo Bank aimed to enhance financial services, offering customers greater convenience in conducting transactions in the digital era.

This approach integrates the Allo Bank Mobile Banking application with a network of physical service points, including TransMart, Metro, Mitra Bukalapak, and Indomaret, ensuring seamless and accessible banking services.

# KINERJA LINGKUNGAN KEBERLANJUTAN

Industri perbankan memiliki peran yang sangat penting dalam menangani permasalahan lingkungan, terutama dalam konteks perubahan iklim yang semakin mendesak. Dengan kapasitasnya untuk mengalokasikan sumber daya keuangan, bank dapat mempengaruhi keputusan investasi yang berdampak langsung pada lingkungan. Melalui penerapan prinsip-prinsip Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), sektor perbankan tidak hanya dapat mengelola risiko yang berkaitan dengan lingkungan, tetapi juga berkontribusi pada upaya keberlanjutan yang lebih luas. Misalnya, Bank dapat memilih untuk mendanai proyek-proyek ramah lingkungan, seperti energi terbarukan dan inisiatif pengurangan emisi karbon sehingga membantu mencapai target Net Zero Emission pada tahun 2060 atau lebih cepat.

Seiring dengan itu, perhatian bank terhadap masalah lingkungan juga menjadi faktor penting dalam menjaga reputasi dan kepercayaan nasabah. Dalam era di mana nasabah semakin sadar akan isu-isu keberlanjutan, bank yang abai terhadap tanggung jawab sosial dan lingkungan berisiko kehilangan kepercayaan dari klien, investor dan segenap pemangku kepentingan lainnya.

# SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE

The banking industry plays a crucial role in addressing environmental challenges, particularly in the face of intensifying climate change. With its capacity to allocate financial resources, banks have the power to influence investment decisions that directly impact the environment. By integrating Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, banks can not only mitigate environmental risks but also contribute to broader sustainability initiatives. For example, banks can prioritize funding for environmentally friendly projects such as renewable energy and carbon emission reduction programs, thereby helping to achieve the Net Zero Emission target by 2060 or earlier.

At the same time, banks' commitment to environmental issues is increasingly becoming a key factor in maintaining customer trust and corporate reputation. In an era where sustainability awareness is growing, banks that fail to uphold social and environmental responsibilities risk losing the confidence of clients, investors, and other stakeholders. Conversely, weak ESG practices can lead to

# Komitmen Allo Bank

Allo Bank mendukung penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan di Indonesia dengan melakukan penyesuaian sejumlah kebijakan agar selaras dengan komitmen mengutamakan nilai Lingkungan (Environmental), Sosial (Social), dan Tata Kelola (Governance) atas ESG. Penyesuaian yang dilakukan antara lain melakukan pembaruan kebijakan penyaluran kredit, serta pembaruan Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) kredit terkait penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan.

Secara spesifik, Bank juga mulai mencanangkan program-program berkelanjutan terkait aspek environment dan social. Dalam hal ini, Bank menjadikan kelompok-kelompok usaha yang mengedepankan bisnis berkelanjutan sebagai target dan sasaran pemberian kredit. Sejalan dengan itu, secara internal, Bank secara optimal menerapkan operasional kantor yang ramah lingkungan dengan memegang prinsip 3R (Reduce, Reuse, & Recycle). Prinsip ini diwujudkan melalui pengelolaan yang baik terkait penggunaan bahan baku/material kertas, energi (bahan bakar minyak dan listrik), air serta limbah.

long-term consequences, such as higher credit risk and financial losses due to climate change. Given these realities, the banking industry must integrate environmental considerations into its decision-making processes to ensure business sustainability and long-term reputational strength.

The demand for the banking industry to contribute to environmental sustainability is an implementation of Republic of Indonesia Law No. 10 of 1998 concerning Amendments to Law No. 7 of 1992 on Banking, which regulates the principle of prudence in credit distribution; Republic of Indonesia Law No. 32 of 2009 on Environmental Protection and Management, where in Article 43, paragraph (3), letter c, there is a clause stating, "Development of an environmentally friendly financial institution and capital market system"; and the Financial Services Authority Regulation No. 51/POJK.03/2017 concerning the Implementation of Sustainable Finance for Financial Services Institutions, Issuers, and Public Companies (POJK Sustainable Finance), released by the Financial Services Authority.

Based on these regulations, the banking sector in Indonesia is required to implement the principles of sustainable finance. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) states that sustainable finance consists of four dimensions: achieving industrial, social, and economic excellence to reduce the threat of global warming and prevent environmental and social issues; shifting targets towards a competitive low-carbon economy; promoting environmentally friendly investments across various business and economic sectors; and supporting the implementation of Indonesia's 4P development principles (pro-growth, pro-jobs, pro-poor, and pro-environment).

Allo Bank actively supports the implementation of sustainable finance in Indonesia by adjusting several policies to align with its commitment to prioritizing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) values. # Pengelolaan Bahan Baku/Material Kertas [OJK F.5]

Allo Bank, sebagai institusi perbankan berbasis digital, masih membutuhkan kertas untuk keperluan administratif. Meskipun demikian, Bank telah mengambil langkah-langkah signifikan untuk meminimalkan penggunaan kertas yang bahan bakunya berasal dari pohon yang diproses menjadi pulp. Upaya penghematan kertas antara lain dilakukan dengan mengoptimalkan penggunaan soft copy atau melalui media surell.

Inisiatif pengurangan penggunaan kertas ini secara tidak langsung berkontribusi pada pelestarian lingkungan dan mengurangi penebangan pohon.

Sejalan dengan itu, Allo Bank juga telah mengimplementasikan DigiSign, solusi tanda tangan elektronik yang menawarkan berbagai manfaat termasuk peningkatan efisiensi yang memungkinkan manajemen menandatangani dokumen secara elektronik dengan aman dan nyaman, menghemat waktu serta mengurangi kesalahan yang terkait dengan tanda tangan manual. Selain menghemat biaya dan mempromosikan kebijakan ramah lingkungan, implementasi tanda tangan digital juga menghilangkan kebutuhan akan tanda tangan berbasis kertas, sekaligus menghemat biaya pencetakan, pengiriman, dan penyimpanan.

Penggunaan kertas di Allo Bank menghasilkan limbah kertas berupa dokumen yang sudah tidak terpakai, meski volumenya tidak signifikan. Untuk mengolah limbah kertas, Bank menyerahkan kepada pihak ketiga untuk didaur ulang (recycle) atau digunakan kembali (reuse). Walaupun kertas termasuk bahan baku/material yang bisa didaur ulang, namun Bank tidak menggunakan hasil daur ulang tersebut dalam operasional sehari-hari

Per 31 Desember 2024, Bank menggunakan kertas sebanyaksebanyak 287 rim, naik dibandingkan tahun 2023 yang mencapai 268 rim. Kenaikan dipengaruhi oleh pelaksanaan pemenuhan Sertifikasi BSMR yang memerlukan kelengkapan dokumen peserta.

# Raw Material Management in Paper [OJK F.5]

As a digital banking institution, Allo Bank still requires paper for administrative purposes. However, the Bank has taken significant steps to minimize paper consumption, particularly since its raw materials come from tree-derived pulp. Efforts to reduce paper usage include optimizing soft copy documentation and email correspondence.

This initiative indirectly contributes to environmental conservation by reducing deforestation.

In line with this, Allo Bank has implemented DigiSign, an electronic signature solution that enhances efficiency by enabling secure and convenient digital document signing. This solution saves time, minimizes errors associated with manual signatures, reduces costs, and eliminates the need for physical paper-based signatures, thereby cutting down on printing, shipping, and storage expenses.

Despite its efforts to reduce paper usage, Allo Bank still generates paper waste, primarily from unused documents, although the volume remains minimal. To manage this waste, the Bank partners with third-party recycling companies. While paper is a recyclable material, Allo Bank does not reuse recycled paper in its daily operations.

As of December 31, 2024, Allo Bank consumed 287 reams of paper, up from 268 reams in 2023. The increase was primarily driven by the implementation of BSMR Certification, which required comprehensive participant documentation.

# Energy Management

Allo Bank relies on two primary energy sources to support its business operations: electricity and fuel (BBM), both supplied by third parties. Electricity is used for lighting and powering various electronic equipment and office facilities, including computers, laptops, photocopiers, air conditioners, and others. Meanwhile, fuel is essential for operational vehicles and as a backup energy source for generators in case of power supply disruptions.

# Pengelolaan Emisi Gas Rumah Kaca

Emisi gas rumah kaca (GRK) merupakan salah satu penyebab terjadinya pemanasan global dan perubahan iklim yang berdampak negatif bagi bumi dan kehidupan di atasnya. Untuk mengurangi dampak tersebut antara lain Allo Bank melakukan penghematan penggunaan energi baik listrik maupun bahan bakar minyak sebagai sumber emisi.

Dalam laporan ini, emisi yang dilaporkan adalah emisi GRK langsung (cakupan 1) yang dihasilkan dari penggunaan bahan bakar fosil (bio solar) dan emisi GRK (cakupan 2) tidak langsung yang bersumber

Reflecting on the fact that fuel and electricity are non-renewable energy sources with limited availability, and that more than half of power plants still rely on coal, the Bank consistently promotes efficient use of both energy types. Electricity efficiency is achieved by optimizing the use of energy-saving LED lamps, turning off lights, air conditioners, and other electronic equipment after office hours, and scheduling power shutdowns at specific times. Meanwhile, fuel efficiency is carried out through strict monitoring of fuel consumption for operational and official vehicles. Additionally, the Bank promotes virtual meetings by utilizing advanced information technology applications for certain types of meetings, thereby reducing the need for transportation, including the use of official vehicles.

These energy-saving initiatives align with Presidential Instruction No. 13 of 2011 on Energy and Water Conservation and Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources Regulation No. 13 of 2012 on Electricity Consumption Reduction. Moreover, these efforts support Allo Bank's commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, a key factor in global warming and climate change. [OJK F.7, F.8]

As of December 31, 2024, Allo Bank's electricity consumption totaled 389,000 kWh, calculated by dividing the electricity bill payment of IDR972.5 million by the electricity tariff for class I-4 at peak hours of IDR2,500 per kWh. This amount marked an increase from 71,720 kWh in 2023, which was determined using the same formula based on an electricity bill payment of IDR179.3 million. The increase was primarily due to the electricity demand for the new Allo Bank Data Center infrastructure, which was inaugurated in May 2024.

Meanwhile, gasoline consumption in 2024 reached 26,610 liters, calculated by dividing total gasoline expenses of IDR368.9 million by the average price of RON95 gasoline (IDR13,864 per liter), which is considered a more environmentally friendly option. This figure rose compared to 16,272 liters in 2023, derived using the same formula with total gasoline expenses of IDR225.6 million. The increase was driven primarily by a 27.37% rise in the number of employees in 2024. [OJK F.6]

## Pengelolaan Air

Air bersih merupakan salah satu kebutuhan vital dalam operasional Allo Bank, terkhusus untuk memenuhi keperluan domestik karyawan seperti air minum, mencuci peralatan dapur, wudhu, pembilasan di kamar kecil, mencuci kendaraan dan sebagainya. Bank mendapatkan air bersih dari pihak ketiga, yaitu produsen air dalam kemasan serta Perusahaan Daerah Air Minum (PDAM).

Sejalan dengan terus berkurangnya pasokan sumber air bersih, termasuk semakin banyaknya polutan pada air permukaan

Meanwhile, indirect GHG emissions (Scope 2) from electricity consumption are calculated by multiplying total electricity usage (in kWh per year) by the average grid emission factor issued by the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, which references the 2015-2024 PLN RUPTL. The emission factor used for Java-Bali is 0.929 kgCO2/kWh (2017). Using this formula, Scope 2 emissions in 2024 totaled 361,381 kgCO2eq (361 tons CO2eq), compared to 66,627 kgCO2eq (67 tons CO2eq) in 2023. This increase is in line with the higher electricity consumption.

As a result, as of December 31, 2024, Allo Bank's total GHG emissions amounted to 422,365 kgCO2eq (422 tons CO2eq), a significant increase compared to 104,049 kgCO2eq (104 tons CO2eq) in 2023.

## Pengelolaan Limbah/Sampah

Operasional Allo Bank menghasilkan limbah, baik cair maupun padat, termasuk kategori Bahan Berbahaya dan Beracun (B3) maupun non-B3. Limbah B3 antara lain berupa aki bekas dan oli bekas dari kendaraan operasional, serta lampu bekas, cartridge bekas, maupun elektronik bekas dari operasional perkantoran. Adapun limbah non-B3 antara lain berupa sampah domestik dari aktivitas karyawan, baik berupa sampah organik maupun non-organik.

Terkhusus pengelolaan sampah perkantoran, selain menyediakan tempat sampah dengan jumlah yang cukup, dan memisahkan sampah berdasarkan jenisnya, Bank bekerja sama dengan pihak ketiga untuk mengangkut sampah tersebut ke tempat pembuangan akhir. Sejalan dengan itu, untuk mengurangi volume sampah, Bank menerapkan sejumlah kebijakan dengan berpatokan pada prinsip 3R (Reduce, Reuse, dan Recycle). Upaya untuk mengurangi limbah plastik air minum dalam kemasan atau kemasan plastik sekali pakai misalnya, Bank menerapkan kebijakan dengan menyediakan pitcher kaca sebagai tempat air minum dan tidak menyediakan air minum dalam kemasan. Bank juga menerapkan spirit green living dengan mengurangi penggunaan tempat makan/minum sekali pakai. Adapun pengelolaan limbah B3, Bank bekerja sama dengan pihak ketiga yang berizin sehingga keberadaan limbah tersebut tidak berdampak negatif bagi lingkungan.

## Waste Management

Allo Bank's operations generate both liquid and solid waste, including hazardous and toxic materials (B3) and non-B3 waste. B3 waste includes used batteries, used oil from operational vehicles, used lamps, used printer cartridges, and discarded electronics from office operations. Non-B3 waste includes domestic waste from employee activities, consisting of organic and non-organic waste.

Specifically for office waste management, in addition to providing sufficient trash bins and segregating waste by type, the Bank collaborates with third-party services for waste collection and disposal. To further reduce waste volume, the Bank implements policies based on the 3R principle (Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle). For instance, to reduce plastic waste from bottled water and single-use plastic packaging, the Bank provides glass pitchers for drinking water and eliminates bottled drinking water. Additionally, the Bank reduces the use of disposable food and beverage containers as part of its green living initiative. For B3 waste management, the Bank partners with licensed third-party providers to ensure that waste disposal does not negatively impact the environment.

# SUSTAINABLE SOCIAL PERFORMANCE

Allo Bank's strong performance, including reaching 11 million customers in its third year, reflects the immense support from stakeholders for the Bank's growth. ## Kesetaraan Kesempatan Kerja [OJK F.18]

Allo Bank secara konsisten menerapkan lingkungan kerja yang adil dan setara tanpa diskriminasi bagi semua karyawan, serta mendukung keberagaman sebagai bagian dari kekuatan Bank. Komitmen tersebut diberlakukan sejak proses rekrutmen dan berlaku untuk semua karyawan existing, baik terkait dengan pelatihan dan pengembangan kompetensi, karir, remunerasi, dan sebagainya. Selaras dengan komitmen tersebut, Bank memberikan kesempatan yang sama dan setara kepada seluruh karyawan laki-laki dan perempuan untuk bekerja, menit karier dan menempati posisi-posisi penting, termasuk di jajaran top management. Prinsip kesetaraan dan non-diskriminasi dalam kesempatan kerja di Allo Bank diatur melalui regulasi internal yaitu Code of Conduct dan Peraturan Perusahaan.

Penerapan kesetaraan kesempatan bekerja di Allo Bank selaras dengan spirit Pasal 28 I ayat (2) Undang-Undang Dasar Negara Republik Indonesia Tahun 1945, yaitu: "Setiap orang berhak bebas dari perlakuan yang bersifat diskriminatif atas dasar apapun dan berhak mendapatkan perlindungan terhadap perlakuan yang bersifat diskriminatif itu." Selain itu, juga sesuai dengan Undang-Undang Republik Indonesia No. 7 Tahun 1984 tentang Pengesahan Konvensi Mengenai Penghapusan Segala Bentuk Diskriminasi terhadap Wanita (Convention On The Elimination Of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women), serta Instruksi Presiden Republik Indonesia No. 9 Tahun 2000 tentang Pengarusutamaan Gender dalam Pembangunan Nasional.

## Tenaga Kerja Anak dan Kerja Paksa [OJK F.19]

Tenaga kerja anak dan kerja paksa merupakan pelanggaran hak asasi manusia yang harus dihapuskan. Sejalan dengan spirit tersebut, maka Allo Bank menetapkan secara jelas batas minimal usia karyawan dan jam kerja. Untuk usia minimal karyawan, Bank memastikan seluruh karyawan, baik tetap maupun kontrak, telah berusia di atas 18 tahun. Dengan ketentuan seperti itu, maka setiap karyawan memiliki waktu istirahat yang cukup. ## Equal Employment Opportunity [OJK F.18]

Allo Bank consistently upholds a fair and equal working environment, ensuring no discrimination among employees and embracing diversity as a key strength of the Bank. This commitment is implemented from the recruitment process and applies to all employees, covering training and competency development, career progression, remuneration, and other employment aspects. In line with this commitment, the Bank provides equal opportunities for both male and female employees to work, advance their careers, and hold key positions, including top management roles. The principles of equality and non-discrimination in employment at Allo Bank are regulated through internal policies, including the Code of Conduct and Company Regulations.

The implementation of equal employment opportunities at Allo Bank aligns with Article 28I, paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, which states: "Everyone has the right to be free from discriminatory treatment on any basis and has the right to receive protection against such discriminatory treatment." Additionally, this commitment complies with Law No. 7 of 1984 concerning the Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women and Presidential Instruction No. 9 of 2000 regarding Gender Mainstreaming in National Development.

## Child Labor and Forced Labor [OJK F.19]

Child labor and forced labor are human rights violations that must be eliminated. In line with this principle, Allo Bank strictly regulates the minimum employment age and working hours. To ensure compliance, the Bank sets the minimum age for all employees, both permanent and contract, at 18 years. This is in accordance with Allo Bank's recruitment policy, which requires candidates to have at least a high school education (or equivalent) and a minimum age of 18 years. The Bank's working hours policy stipulates 8 (eight) hours per day and 40 (forty) hours per week, following a 5-day workweek. This is in line with Article 77 of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower, ensuring that employees have adequate rest periods. Due to these strict regulations, Allo Bank has effectively prevented any instances of child labor or forced labor.

## Upah Minimum Regional [OJK F.20]

Pemenuhan upah minimum bukan hanya kewajiban hukum bagi Allo Bank, tetapi juga strategi yang penting dalam menciptakan hubungan kerja yang harmonis, meningkatkan produktivitas, dan memastikan keberlanjutan perusahaan. Untuk itu, dalam pemberian upah, Bank berupaya semaksimal mungkin memenuhi kriteria keadilan agar memacu semangat karyawan untuk bekerja dan berprestasi. Selaras dengan kepatuhan terhadap regulasi terkait upah, terkhusus remunerasi bagi karyawan tetap di tingkat terendah, Bank memberikan upah minimum dengan tetap memperhatikan pemenuhan kebutuhan hidup layak. Besaran upah minimum diberikan dengan menyesuaikan harga kebutuhan pokok, tingkat inflasi, standar kelayakan hidup, dan variabel lainnya, sebagaimana ditentukan oleh pemerintah. Contribution to Financial Literacy and Inclusion

Financial literacy and inclusion play a vital role in enhancing public understanding of financial products and services, enabling individuals to make wiser decisions in financial management. Recognizing this, the government mandates financial service institutions, including banks, to actively promote financial inclusion through various programs and initiatives. According to Financial Services Authority Regulation No. 76/POJK.07/2016 on Financial Literacy and Inclusion in the Financial Services Sector, financial literacy refers to knowledge, skills, and confidence that influence an individual's behavior and decision-making in managing finances to achieve financial well-being. Meanwhile, financial inclusion refers to the availability of access to diverse financial institutions, products, and services tailored to the needs and capabilities of the community to improve their overall welfare.

Hasil survei kolaborasi dua lembaga yang diumumkan pada awal Agustus 2024 menyebutkan indeks literasi keuangan masyarakat sebesar 65,43% dan inklusi keuangan 75,02%.

Pengumpulan data SNLIK 2024 dilakukan pada 9 Januari-5 Februari 2024 di 34 provinsi yang mencakup 120 kabupaten/kota termasuk 8 wilayah kantor OJK (1.080 blok sensus). Jumlah sampel SNLIK tahun 2024 sebanyak 10.800 responden yang berumur antara 15-79 tahun.

OJK dan BPS menegaskan indeks literasi dan inklusi keuangan hasil SNLIK 2024 tidak dapat langsung dibandingkan secara langsung terhadap indeks literasi dan inklusi keuangan hasil tahun 2022. Sebab, metodologi sampling untuk SNLIK 2024 berbeda dengan SNLIK 2022. Dalam SNLIK 2024 metodologi sampling yang digunakan adalah stratified multistage cluster sampling yang lebih mampu merepresentasikan tingkat literasi dan inklusi keuangan masyarakat secara keseluruhan. Adapun SNLIK 2022 menggunakan metodologi purposive sampling dan simple random sampling yang menghasilkan sampel responden yang cenderung bias ke perkotaan dan kelompok masyarakat berpendidikan tinggi. Merujuk hasil SNLIK 2022, indeks literasi keuangan masyarakat tercatat sebesar 49,68%, sedangkan indeks inklusi keuangan mencapai 85,10%.

Lebih lanjut, hasil SNLIK 2024 menunjukkan bahwa berdasarkan gender, indeks literasi keuangan perempuan lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan indeks literasi keuangan laki-laki, yakni masing-masing sebesar 66,75% dan 64,14%. Indeks inklusi keuangan perempuan juga lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan indeks inklusi keuangan laki-laki, yakni masing-masing 76,08% dan 73,97%. Sementara itu, berdasarkan klasifikasi desa, indeks literasi dan inklusi keuangan wilayah perkotaan masing-masing sebesar 69,71% dan 78,41%, lebih tinggi dibandingkan di wilayah perdesaan yakni masing-masing sebesar 59,25% dan 70,13%.

Berdasarkan umur, kelompok 26-35 tahun, 36-50 tahun, dan 18-25 tahun memiliki indeks literasi keuangan tertinggi, yakni masing-masing sebesar 74,82%, 71,72%, dan 70,19%. Sebaliknya, kelompok umur 15-17 tahun dan 51-79 tahun memiliki indeks literasi keuangan terendah, yakni masing-masing sebesar 51,70% dan 52,51%. Kemudian, kelompok umur 26-35 tahun, 36-50 tahun, dan 18-25 tahun memiliki indeks inklusi keuangan tertinggi, yakni masing-masing sebesar 84,28%, 81,51%, dan 79,21% Namun demikian, kelompok umur 15-17 tahun dan 51-79 tahun memiliki indeks inklusi keuangan terendah, yakni masing-masing sebesar 57,96% dan 63,53%.

To assess the financial literacy and inclusion index, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) and the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) conducted the 2024 National Financial Literacy and Inclusion Survey (SNLIK) for the first time. The survey results, announced in early August 2024, reported a financial literacy index of 65.43% and a financial inclusion index of 75.02%.

The SNLIK 2024 data collection took place from January 9 to February 5, 2024, across 34 provinces and 120 districts/cities, covering 1,080 census blocks under 8 OJK regional offices. The survey sampled 10,800 respondents aged 15-79 years.

OJK and BPS emphasized that the financial literacy and inclusion index from SNLIK 2024 cannot be directly compared to the SNLIK 2022 results due to differences in sampling methodologies. The 2024 survey used a stratified multistage cluster sampling method, which provides a more comprehensive and representative measure of financial literacy and inclusion across various demographic groups. In contrast, the 2022 survey used purposive sampling and simple random sampling methods, which tended to be biased toward urban and highly educated respondents. For reference, the 2022 SNLIK results recorded a financial literacy index of 49.68% and a financial inclusion index of 85.10%.

Furthermore, the results of the 2024 SNLIK indicate that, based on gender, the women's financial literacy index is higher than the men's financial literacy index, at 66.75% and 64.14%, respectively. Similarly, the women's financial inclusion index surpasses that of men, standing at 76.08% compared to 73.97%. Meanwhile, based on village classification, the financial literacy and inclusion indexes in urban areas are 69.71% and 78.41%, respectively, which are higher than those in rural areas, at 59.25% and 70.13%, respectively.

From an age group perspective, the 26-35, 36-50, and 18-25 age groups have the highest financial literacy indexes, at 74.82%, 71.72%, and 70.19%, respectively. In contrast, the 15-17 and 51-79 age groups record the lowest financial literacy indexes, at 51.70% and 52.51%, respectively. Similarly, the 26-35, 36-50, and 18-25 age groups exhibit the highest financial inclusion indexes, at 84.28%, 81.51%, and 79.21%, respectively. However, the 15-17 and 51-79 age groups have the lowest financial inclusion indexes, at 57.96% and 63.53%, respectively.

In compliance with POJK No. 3 of 2023 concerning Increasing Literacy and Financial Inclusion in the Financial Services Sector for Consumers and the Community in the Financial Services Sector and POJK No. 22 of 2023 concerning Consumer and Public Protection

## Kerugian Kredit Ekspektasian ("KKE") - Cadangan Kerugian Penurunan Nilai atas Kredit yang Diberikan

Seperti yang dijelaskan dalam Catatan 10 (Kredit yang diberikan) atas laporan keuangan pada tanggal 31 Desember 2024, total kredit yang diberikan sebesar Rp7.478.035 juta dengan cadangan kerugian penurunan nilai sebesar Rp104.484 juta.

Cadangan kerugian penurunan nilai atas kredit yang diberikan ditentukan Bank berdasarkan kerangka kerugian kredit ekspektasian ("KKE") sesuai dengan PSAK 109: Instrumen Keuangan, seperti yang dijelaskan dalam Catatan 2.k (i) (Penurunan nilai aset keuangan) atas laporan keuangan.

Kami fokus pada area ini karena signifikansi nilai tercatat atas kredit yang diberikan, yang mewakili 53,5% dari jumlah aset Bank pada tanggal 31 Desember 2024 dan besarnya nilai cadangan kerugian penurunan nilai yang dibentuk atas kredit tersebut nilainya signifikan terhadap laporan keuangan Bank. Lebih lanjut, penentuan KKE membutuhkan pertimbangan manajemen yang subjektif dan melibatkan penggunaan estimasi dengan tingkat ketidakpastian yang tinggi.

Bank menghitung KKE untuk kredit yang diberikan yang tidak memburuk dan kredit yang diberikan yang memburuk. Untuk kredit yang diberikan yang tidak memburuk dan kredit yang diberikan yang memburuk, yang secara individual tidak dianggap signifikan, Bank menghitung KKE secara kolektif menggunakan model KKE dengan beberapa asumsi utama, antara lain probability of default, loss given default, dan exposure at default, setelah memperhitungkan faktor masa depan dan informasi eksternal lainnya.

# Key Audit Matters

Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgment, were of most significance in our audit of the financial statements of the current period. These matters were addressed in the context of our audit of the financial statements as a whole, and in forming our opinion thereon, and we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters.

The key audit matter identified in our audit is outlined as follows:

## Expected Credit Losses ("ECL") - Allowance for Impairment Losses of Loans

As described in Notes 10 (Loans) to the financial statements as of December 31, 2024, the total loans amounted to Rp7,478,035 million with allowance for impairment losses of loans amounted to Rp104,484 million.

The allowance for impairment losses of loans is determined by the Bank based on the Expected Credit Losses ("ECL") framework under PSAK 109: Financial Instrument, as described in Notes 2.k (i) (Impairment of financial assets) to the financial statements.

We focused on this area as the total loans represents 53.5% of the total assets of the Bank as of December 31, 2024, and the allowance for impairment losses provided against the loans were significant to the Bank's financial statements. Furthermore, determining ECL involves subjective management judgement and is subject to a high degree of estimation uncertainty.

The Bank calculated ECL for both non-impaired loans and impaired loans. For non-impaired loans and impaired loans which are not considered individually significant, the Bank assesses collective ECL using the ECL modelling approach that incorporates key assumptions, including probability of default, loss given default, and exposure at default, after considering forward-looking factors and other external information.

## Bagaimana audit kami merespons hal audit utama

Kami melakukan prosedur-prosedur audit berikut untuk merespons hal audit utama ini:

1. Kami memperoleh pemahaman atas pendekatan Bank dalam mengidentifikasi kredit yang diberikan yang mengalami peningkatan risiko kredit secara signifikan atau bukti objektif penurunan nilai, dan melakukan pengujian, berdasarkan uji petik, kesesuaian dari klasifikasi kualitas kredit yang diberikan dengan menelaah dokumen kredit dari debitur-debitur yang menjadi sampel, serta membuat penilaian independen kami apakah ada peningkatan risiko kredit secara signifikan atau terdapat bukti objektif penurunan nilai.

2. Kami menilai kecukupan cadangan kerugian penurunan nilai yang dihitung secara individual dengan menguji, berdasarkan uji petik, kecukupan cadangan kerugian penurunan nilai yang dihitung oleh manajemen, dengan mengevaluasi kesesuaian estimasi probabilitas rata-rata tertimbang kerugian kredit yang diberikan, serta estimasi waktu dan jumlah pembayaran dari kredit yang diberikan, yang diterapkan oleh Bank dalam mengestimasi arus kas ekspektasian dari kredit yang diberikan.

3. Kami menilai metodologi dan menguji asumsi permodelan signifikan yang digunakan dalam model KKE kolektif, dengan bantuan pakar permodelan kredit kami. Kami menguji probability of default, loss given default dan exposure at default, yang mencakup (i) evaluasi prakiraan makroekonomi Indonesia dengan membandingkan prakiraan dengan informasi yang tersedia untuk umum tentang prospek makroekonomi Indonesia; dan (ii) menguji kelengkapan dan keakuratan data yang digunakan dalam model dengan data aktual yang tersedia di Bank.

4. Kami melakukan perhitungan ulang dan menguji, berdasarkan uji petik, akurasi perhitungan KKE yang dinilai secara kolektif dan individual.

For impaired loans, which are considered individually significant, the Bank assesses individual ECL by estimating the expected cash flows obtained from the loans, which requires significant judgement in estimating the weighted average probability of credit losses, and the timing and amount of the repayments against the loans.

## How our audit addresses the key audit matter

We have performed the following audit procedures to address this key audit matter:

1. We understood the Bank's approach over the identification of financial assets that have experienced a significant increase in credit risk or objective evidence of impairment, and tested, on a sample basis, the appropriateness of the credit quality classification by reviewing the credit files of those sampled debtors, and formed our own independent judgement as to whether there was a significant increase in credit risk or any objective evidence of impairment.

2. We assessed the adequacy of individual allowance for impairment losses by testing, on a sample basis, the adequacy of the allowance for impairment losses calculated by management, by evaluating the appropriateness of weighted average probability of credit losses, and the timing and amount of the repayments against the loans, which were applied by the Bank in estimating the expected cash flow obtained from the loans.

3. We assessed the methodologies applied and tested the significant modelling assumptions used in collective ECL models, with assistance from our credit modelling expert. We tested probability of default, loss given default and exposure at default, which included (i) evaluating the forecasts of Indonesia macroeconomics by comparing forecasts with publicly available information on the Indonesia macroeconomic outlook; and (ii) testing the completeness and accuracy of data used in the model with the actual data available within the Bank.

4. We recalculated and tested, on a sample basis, the accuracy of the collective and individual ECL calculation.
